name: Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit
story: Not really an orbit around the Moon — more like a long figure-8 around the Earth-Moon L1 and L2 Lagrange points, dipping close to the lunar south pole at perilune (~3,000 km) and stretching far above the north pole at apolune (~70,000 km). The geometry has two prizes: continuous line-of-sight back to Earth (no comms blackout) and very low station-keeping fuel — a few m/s per year. NASA's Lunar Gateway, when it flies, will live in NRHO. CAPSTONE flew there in 2022 as a pathfinder.
comparison: An NRHO completes one loop every ~6.5 days — roughly a quarter of the Moon's own orbital period. The spacecraft is always close to the south-pole region but never directly above it.
